text:
Alex Wu: quick heads-up — ran the slab-aware allocator + kernel routing sweep on canary. seeing a P95 tail regression when KV occupancy climbs above ~75%.
Priya Nair: can you share the numbers and config you used?
Alex Wu: summary from perf-bot below, full trace linked. key bits: slab allocator does more eager packing which increases simultaneous KV footprints; kernel-alpha has a higher per-seq-kv allocation which seems to push us into eviction churn.
perf-bot: run summary: requests=10k, model=redwood-rlm-medium, batcher=slab-aware-v1, kernel_routing=alpha->beta fallback, kv_occupancy=0.78, p50=48ms, p95=420ms (+35% vs baseline), throughput= -2.1%, OOMs=0. trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/abcd1234
Alex Wu: config snippet used:
```
batching:
  allocator: slab
  token_budget_target: 1024
  kv_reserve_ratio: 0.22
kernel_routing:
  prefer_low_mem: true
  fallback: kernel-beta
```
Samir Patel: do we have a flamegraph or allocation breakdown for kernel-alpha? curious if the extra KV is coming from per-layer buffers or some transient staging.
Alex Wu: flamegraph attached in the trace — kernel-alpha spikes on layer 10-12 KV accumulation for long-context requests. looks like eager read-around in the attention kernel.
Kevin Zhou: hypothesis: the allocator is packing more requests into the same batch which increases peak concurrent KV slices; combined with alpha's staging it crosses the soft-eviction watermark. If we increase kv_reserve_ratio to 0.30 p95 drops but throughput falls ~4%.
Marisol Vega: is this a regression introduced by kernel-alpha changes or by the slab allocator tweak?
Alex Wu: it's an interaction. before allocator change we rarely saw occupancy >70% for this workload. slab packing made batches denser so memory peaks higher. kernel-alpha's attention change amplified it.
Priya Nair: proposed quick experiments:
  A) token_budget_target -> 1536 (looser batching)
  B) kv_reserve_ratio -> 0.35
  C) prefer kernel-beta earlier (route to low-mem kernels when est_kv > threshold)
Samir Patel: also add telemetry in admission path: record est_kv(request), current_kv_occupancy, decision_reason. we need to know why something gets admitted vs routed.
Alex Wu: agree. provisional soft-admission pseudo: 
```
if kv_occupancy + est_kv(req) > headroom_threshold:
  route_to_kernel_beta(req)  # lower-memory kernel or lower-density batch
else:
  admit_to_batch(req)
```
Alex Wu: running A and C first, will update.
perf-bot: run 1769994321_2 results: requests=10k, token_budget=1536 + prefer-beta routing, p50=52ms, p95=310ms (-26% vs previous), throughput=-3.0%, OOMs=0, dropped_routes=2.
Kevin Zhou: nice, makes sense. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: after Alex's next run can we add the admission logging and re-run the same trace so we can correlate request attributes -> routing decisions?
Alex Wu: yes i'll add logging (small perf cost) and schedule another sweep tomorrow morning.
Marisol Vega: note for release notes: call out interaction risk between dense packing allocators and kernels with staging buffers. gives ops a knob (kv_reserve_ratio / prefer_low_mem) to mitigate.
Priya Nair: thanks Alex — pls post the logs and the admission decisions once you have them.
Alex Wu: will do.
